info.title: FreeTicket B2B API
info.description:
FreeTicket B2B REST API for integrations, the `ft` CLI and the FreeTicket MCP server. Authentication is by API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` header or `x-api-key`); the active workspace is selected with the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Scopes: each key is either `read` (GET/HEAD only) or `write` (additionally creates, edits, deletes, cancels, refunds and checks in). Self-service keys are issued as `read`. A `read` key calling a mutating method gets a 403. The machine-readable declaration lives at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728).

Getting a key (self-serve, no sales contact): `ft login` runs the Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628, `POST /auth/device/code` + `POST /auth/device/token`); the user approves the code at https://admin.appfreeticket.com/device and the CLI receives a key. New organizers can bootstrap headless with `POST /auth/signup` (verify-first, then `ft login`). With a key, `POST /api-keys` mints more (born `read` unless `write` is requested). There is no sandbox environment: test against a dedicated workspace with `read` keys.

## Versioning and deprecation

- **Path version.** The B2B API is versioned in the path (`/api/v1`). A breaking change ships under a new path (`/api/v2`); the previous version keeps running in parallel until its sunset date.
- **Contract version.** `info.version` is the semantic version of this document. MINOR = additive (new endpoints, new optional fields, new enum values, new error codes; clients must ignore unknown fields). PATCH = documentation or fixes that do not change shapes. The public API (`/api/public`) is pre-1.0 and not versioned in the path: there, a MINOR bump may include a breaking change and PATCH never does.
- **Deprecation signals.** A deprecated operation is marked `deprecated: true` in this document and its responses carry `Deprecation` (RFC 9745, e.g. `Deprecation: @1767225600`), `Sunset` (RFC 8594, an HTTP-date after which the operation may stop working) and `Link: <https://appfreeticket.com/desarrolladores>; rel="deprecation"`.
- **Timeline.** At least 6 months between the first `Deprecation` header and the `Sunset` date for `/api/v1`, and at least 90 days for `/api/public`. A path version is only retired after all its operations have sunset.
- **Current status.** No operation is deprecated today.

## Rate limits

- **429 always carries `Retry-After`** (seconds). Wait at least that long before retrying the same request. The JSON error envelope comes with `error.retryable: true`; most rate-limited responses use `error.code: "RATE_LIMITED"`, and some return a more specific code (for example `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` or `SEAT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`).
- **RateLimit headers are sent where listed below.** Those endpoints answer every response, success or error, with the IETF RateLimit headers (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `RateLimit-Policy: "<policy>";q=<quota>;w=<window seconds>` and `RateLimit: "<policy>";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds until reset>`. Other endpoints may answer 429 without them.
- Counters are fixed windows kept per server instance: treat the numbers as pacing hints, not as a global account quota.

Endpoints that send RateLimit headers today: `POST /auth/signup` (per client IP), `POST /customer/auth/request` and `POST /customer/auth/verify` (per client IP), and the buyer-session endpoints `GET /customer/orders/{id}`, `POST /customer/orders/{id}/payment`, `/payment/card`, `/payment/pse`, `/release`, `POST /customer/purchase-sessions` and `POST /customer/purchase-sessions/{id}/release`.

post.description: Requires a valid API key — does NOT require an active workspace (`X-Workspace-Id` does not apply here: it is ignored if sent). The caller becomes ADMIN of the new workspace. If they already administer their own Organization (umbrella), another workspace is added there, subject to the plan quota (spark=1, star=3, icon=7); if they have no link at all, a new Organization is created on the free Spark plan. A user who is already a collaborator (staff) of someone else's workspace gets 409 `ALREADY_HAS_ACCESS`: ask an administrator to add them, instead of creating a tenant that would override their current access.

post.summary: Publish an event
post.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Publishes the event and its dates (cancelled dates stay cancelled unless the whole event was `CANCELLED`). Requires at least one future date (409 `CONFLICT`).

Seated (seats.io) events are validated first:
- 409 `SEATSIO_INVALID`: a seated date has no ticket type mapped to a chart category, or maps a category missing from the chart.
- 409 `SEAT_MAP_CATEGORIES_UNCOVERED`: a chart category with seats on sale has no ticket type on that date and is not fully blocked (booked). `error.details.zones[]` lists each one (`dateLabel`, `categoryKey`, `categoryLabel`, `seats`). Create its ticket type or block those seats, then retry.
- 503 `SEAT_MAP_UNVERIFIABLE` (retryable): seats.io could not be reached to verify the map.

Paid events (any ticket type with price > 0) require the workspace identity verification to be approved:
- 409 `IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`: the event stays `DRAFT` and is queued; it publishes automatically within ~5 minutes of the verification being approved.

put.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Replaces the artists linked to the event with `artistIds`, in that order (the lineup order). Artists not in the list are unlinked (send the full lineup, not a diff); `[]` clears it. Ids come from `GET /artists?q=` (workspace ids of registered artists). Newly linked artists get a notification email.

`inviteEmails` invites artists without an account: each email gets an invitation (only once per email and event) and is linked when it signs up. `inviteEmails` is additive: omitting it does not cancel existing invitations (use `DELETE /events/{id}/artist-invitations/{invitationId}`).

Ids that are not a registered artist (or the event's own workspace) are skipped and reported in `warnings[]` with code `ARTIST_IDS_IGNORED` (`ids`).

Limits: up to 50 `artistIds` and 20 `inviteEmails` per request; 20 lineup changes per hour per API key and event (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Cancel a sale (blocked if someone already checked in or the payment is still open)
post.description: Marks the sale as CANCELLED, releases its inventory and frees the associated numbered seats. IMPORTANT: a sale with tickets already used at the door is NOT cancelled: it responds 409 SALE_ALREADY_CHECKED_IN, because returning that inventory would put it back on sale with the person already inside. If the money must be returned, use POST /sales/{id}/refund. IMPORTANT: a PENDING sale charged through Bold has a payment link that may still be live — the Bold API never marks its links as expired —, so cancelling it could leave the buyer charged without a ticket. Before cancelling, the actual payment status is re-read: if Bold reports it approved, it responds 409 SALE_PAID_AT_GATEWAY and the sale is NOT cancelled under any circumstances (that sale gets confirmed or refunded). If the payment is still open or its status cannot be read, it responds 409 OPEN_PAYMENT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED: check the Bold dashboard and repeat the call with {"acknowledge_open_payment": true} to explicitly accept the risk. A sale charged with a Bold card terminal (counter sale) that still has a terminal charge in progress, or an approved charge not yet delivered, responds 409 TERMINAL_CHARGE_IN_PROGRESS and is not cancelled (the acknowledgement does not override it). Sales from other gateways and sales with no payment started are cancelled without that step.

post.summary: Refund a sale (moving the funds depends on the payment gateway)
post.description: Marks the sale as REFUNDED and releases the associated numbered seats. IMPORTANT: whether the money goes back to the buyer depends on the payment gateway and the payment method used. Sales charged through MercadoPago are fully refunded against the MercadoPago API (stable idempotency key per sale, so retries never refund twice) and marked only once MercadoPago confirms. A 503 GATEWAY_REFUND_PENDING means MercadoPago did not answer clearly: the sale stays CONFIRMED and repeating the same call is safe. Sales charged through Wompi by CARD are voided against the payment gateway before being marked. In every other case this endpoint does NOT trigger the actual refund: the money is NOT returned automatically and a 200 only confirms the accounting status change. Those refunds must be handled separately in the payment gateway's dashboard. PARTIAL REFUND BY TICKET: send `items` with the ids of the sale items to refund (the `id` field of GET /sales/{id}/tickets). Each item refunds its prorated share of the sale total (by item subtotal; shares always add up to the exact total). The refunded tickets are invalidated at the door and their quota returns to stock; when no live item remains the sale becomes REFUNDED. Only MercadoPago (or uncharged / cash sales) support partial refunds: Wompi and Bold answer 409 GATEWAY_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED. Items already checked in answer 409 ITEM_ALREADY_CHECKED_IN — also for a FULL refund (no `items`, or all of them): a sale with any checked-in ticket is never refunded whole; refund the unused tickets by item; items from another sale answer 422 ITEM_NOT_IN_SALE; a refund already in flight over the same items answers 409 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS (retry exactly the same items). `block_seats: true` (also valid for a full refund) keeps the refunded numbered seats OUT of sale: seats.io moves them from booked straight to a blocked status, never through free. The `refund` object in the response reports the refunded amount and what happened to the seats. Wompi payment methods without API refunds (PSE, Nequi, Bancolombia transfer) respond 409: return the money in the Wompi dashboard and repeat the call with {"acknowledge_manual": true} to reflect the accounting status. A 502 means the gateway rejected the void and the sale remains CONFIRMED.

patch.summary: Reassign a sold ticket to another date or ticket type
patch.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Moves an ALREADY SOLD ticket to another `ticketTypeId` and/or to the `eventDateId` date (at least one of the two is required). Intended for a postponement: moving buyers from the old date to the new one without refunding and reselling.

With only `eventDateId`, the target ticket type is resolved by NAME (the same type the ticket had, on the new date); if the target date doesn't have exactly one type with that name, it responds 422 and you must pass an explicit `ticketTypeId`.

It does NOT charge or refund the price difference if the new type costs something else: the ticket's `unitPrice`/`subtotal` keep the sale's ORIGINAL price. If money needs adjusting, use `POST /sales/{id}/refund` separately.

It does NOT reissue the QR: `ticketCode` is always preserved (it is what the buyer already has printed, in Wallet and in their email).

It does NOT notify the buyer. This endpoint only moves data; to resend the updated ticket use `POST /tickets/{ticketCode}/resend`, and for a bulk postponement notice, use the communications module.

A ticket that is already checked in, or that belongs to a sale that is not CONFIRMED, responds 409 and is not reassigned. A ticket refunded by item (or whose seat was blocked after a refund) responds 409 `TICKET_REFUNDED`.

NUMBERED SEATING (seats.io): if the target date has numbered seating, `seatLabel` is REQUIRED (409 `SEAT_REQUIRED` if missing) — the server never picks a seat on its own. The seat is validated and booked in seats.io before moving the ticket; if it is no longer available, it responds 409 `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` without changing anything. If the ticket held a numbered seat on the source date, that seat is released after the move is confirmed.

post.summary: Open the purchase session (only one live per buyer)
post.description: Requires the `X-Customer-Session` header. The enterprise service API key is OPTIONAL (with a key, the event date must belong to the workspace pinned to it; otherwise 404). Opens THE buyer purchase session: there is ONLY one live per buyer across any tab or device, and the latest wins — the previous one becomes `superseded` (it can no longer create an order or start a new payment) and its seats.io hold is released, unless it backs a live sale. On seated event dates the server ISSUES the `holdToken` (mount the chart with `session: "manual"`) and sets `seatsDeadline`: each session gets up to 3 minutes and the budget is 3 attempts (9 CUMULATIVE minutes) per buyer and event date, summing all of their sessions within a 30-minute window, and it only runs while no order has been created. Once exhausted, it responds 429 with `error.code` `SEAT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `error.details.reason` `seat_budget_exhausted` and `error.details.retryAfterSeconds` (10-minute cooldown; also in the `Retry-After` header). If the SAME browser (`deviceKey`) reopens the SAME event date with its session alive, it gets that same session with 200 instead of 201. Only event dates on sale: published event and current event date (otherwise 404). Limits: 10 creations per minute per buyer, 30 per minute per IP when called without an API key, and a global ceiling per event date (429 `RATE_LIMITED`). Once the session is created, `POST /customer/orders` and the payment POSTs carry the `X-Purchase-Session: <id>` header; when the clock runs out, call `POST /customer/purchase-sessions/{id}/release`.

Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

sent_to.description: Masked email (`c***@mail.com`). Never the full address.

session_token.description: Usable as-is as the `X-Customer-Session` header on /api/v1/customer/*.

ticketCode.description: Opaque ticket code. The QR code must encode the validator URL (`https://admin.appfreeticket.com/dashboard/tickets/validar?code=<ticketCode>`).

seatLabel.description: Exact seat for seated events (seats.io), or null.

startsAt.description: Event start instant in ISO 8601 UTC.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the event.

revoked.description: true if the session existed and was deleted; false if the token was no longer valid (it ends up closed either way).

token.description: One-time token received on the landing page callback (format `{slug}.{token}`, forwarded as is).

session_token.description: Buyer session token. Send it as the `X-Customer-Session` header on /api/v1/customer/*.

active.description: true only with an ACTIVE, unexpired membership in this workspace.

expiresAt.description: null = LIFETIME or a membership with no expiry.

planId.description: Id of an active MembershipPlan in the key's workspace.

checkoutUrl.description: Membership checkout URL on the canonical host. The landing page must redirect the buyer there.

workspaceId.description: Required only without an enterprise service API key: which membership (by workspace) to cancel. Ignored with a key — the workspace is the one pinned to it.

phone.description: null or an empty string clears the phone.

deviceKey.description: Stable browser identifier (e.g. stored in localStorage). If the SAME browser reopens the SAME event date while its session is still alive, it gets that same session (same `holdToken`, same clock) instead of a new one.

seated.description: true = the event date has a seats.io map.

holdToken.description: seats.io hold token ISSUED BY THE SERVER. Mount the chart with `session: "manual"` and this `holdToken` (https://docs.seats.io/docs/renderer/config-session/), never with `session: "continue"`. It is the ONLY token `POST /customer/orders` accepts for this session. null for event dates without a map.

seatsDeadline.description: Instant (ISO 8601 UTC) until which the order with seats can be created. This is the clock to display over the map. The seats.io hold expires AFTER this instant, never before. null for event dates without a map.

budgetSeconds.description: Budget seconds granted to this session (= seatsDeadline − now). The budget is CUMULATIVE per buyer and event date: opening another tab does not reset it.

replacedSessionId.description: Live session that this one replaced (now `superseded`), or null. That tab can no longer create an order or start a new payment.

state.description: `live`: can create the order. `superseded`: another tab/device replaced it. `expired`: the map clock ran out or it was released. `converted`: it already created its order (`orderId`).

orderId.description: Sale created with this session, if any.

free.description: true = the purchase was CONFIRMED without a payment gateway (100% discount). In that case do NOT call /payment: there is nothing to charge and the other fields are null.

reference.description: Sale reference (FT-…). Always identifies the purchase.

saleId.description: Sale id. null when `free` is true.

total.description: Amount to charge. null when `free` is true.

expiresAt.description: Instant (ISO 8601 UTC) at which the inventory reservation expires. After that, the purchase must be started over.
Instant (ISO 8601 UTC) at which the inventory hold expires. This is the countdown to display.

paymentOpened.description: true = payment has already been opened for this sale. Reopening it with /payment returns the SAME signed configuration while the reservation is still alive.

seatLabel.description: seats.io numbered seat, or null if not seated.

order.description: The purchase the buyer left unfinished for this event date, or null if there is none.

released.description: The sale is now ABANDONED and its inventory went back to stock. A rejection never lands here: it is returned as an error with `details.reason`.

apiKey.description: Bold IDENTITY key (public, sent to the browser).

integritySignature.description: SHA256 that binds the charge to the amount. Computed on the server.

expirationDate.description: Epoch in NANOSECONDS (what the Bold library expects).

publicKey.description: MercadoPago (Tickets) public key. Sent to the browser: it is what `initMercadoPago()`/`<Payment>` from the `@mercadopago/sdk-react` SDK (or equivalent) receives to mount the Payment Brick. Present ONLY on the MercadoPago rail — it is the marker the landing page uses to tell it apart from the Bold rail (which carries `apiKey`+`renderMode` and NEVER `publicKey`).

amount.description: Amount to charge, in the currency's major unit (pesos, not cents) — the same `total` already returned by `POST /customer/orders`. It is re-read from the sale on every call: do not treat it as final if a long time passes between mounting the Brick and charging.

payerEmail.description: Buyer email (from the sale, not editable). Informational: the charge ALWAYS uses the sale's email, never one sent by the client.

token.description: Card token returned by the Payment Brick when tokenizing.

issuerId.description: `issuer_id` returned by the Brick. Some BINs require it.

email.description: Ignored: the charge ALWAYS uses the sale's email, never one sent by the client.

status.description: `pending` is normal: it may require additional authentication from the bank. `rejected` is a business decline (funds, card details, …) — the buyer can retry with another card.

message.description: Human-readable message for the buyer. Only present with `rejected`.

saleAlive.description: Only present with `rejected`. `false`: the purchase was cancelled and its tickets (and seats) went back to inventory — a new purchase must be started. `true`: THIS payment was declined but the purchase is still pending because another payment is in progress on it (e.g. a PSE payment waiting on the bank); do NOT start a new purchase: show the message, wait, and check the order status.

redirectUrl.description: `init_point` of the MercadoPago preference. Redirect the buyer there (it is not an iframe): they pick their bank and confirm the transfer on MercadoPago.

status.description: `pending` is a NORMAL state: Bold may take a while to reflect the payment (PSE, Nequi and the Bancolombia button approve asynchronously) and the webhook settles it. The landing page must retry, not treat the purchase as lost.

tickets.description: Tickets with their `ticketCode`. ONLY present when `status` is `approved`; null in any other case. A code handed out before the payment settles would be a valid ticket with no money behind it.

seats.description: seats.io labels. Only for seated events.

holdToken.description: Hold token of the seats.io map session. Required if seats are sent.

nitDigit.description: Check digit. Required if idType is NIT.

returnUrl.description: Absolute URL of the landing page the buyer returns to. Validated against the enterprise domain allowlist and the workspace that owns the event; if it fails validation it is ignored and the purchase proceeds as usual.

memberOnly.description: true = only current members of the organization can play it.

type.description: TEXT/IMAGE posts only. An ARTICLE stays an ARTICLE (and vice versa).

imageUrl.description: ARTICLE posts: the cover image. null removes it.

channelId.description: TEXT/IMAGE posts only. Active channel of the workspace; null moves it back to Announcements.

publishedAt.description: Reschedules the post (and its member notification, if any).

pinnedAt.description: null when unpinned. At most one pinned post per workspace.

deletedIds.description: The comment plus its live replies (top-level comments).

orderedIds.description: EVERY active channel id, in the new order, Announcements first.

deleted.description: Deleted (by its author or the team) with reports still open.

imageUrl.description: PENDING_REVIEW: short-lived signed URL (the image lives in a private bucket until approved).

updatedAt.description: Version read by the moderator: pass it as `expectedUpdatedAt` to approve.

changed.description: false = it was already in that state (idempotent).

commentId.description: Comment of this member in the workspace that motivates the ban (required: a ban always comes from a reported comment).

hideAllComments.description: true = hide every comment of the member in this workspace, not only `commentId`.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: `updatedAt` of the post as read from `GET /content/moderation/member-posts`.

reason.description: Shown to the author in their inbox.

banAuthor.description: Also bans the author from the community. Requires ADMIN.

onlineUrl.description: ONLINE only; must start with https://

requiresApproval.description: true = the staff approves each RSVP request.

body.description: ARTICLE posts only. Body in Markdown.

readingMinutes.description: ARTICLE posts only. Not redacted when `locked`: it does not leak content, only its length.

link.description: Open Graph snapshot of the first link in the text. Always null for ARTICLE posts.

commentsCount.description: Visible comments: excludes deleted ones and those hidden by moderation (and replies to a hidden comment). 0 if the post arrives redacted.

hasRecording.description: true if a playable recording remains after the stream.

RateLimitPolicy.description: Quota policies applied to this request (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers), one list member per limiter: `"<policy>";q=<quota>;w=<window seconds>`. Example: `"public-orders";q=8;w=300`.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota per policy (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `"<policy>";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds until the window resets>`. Example: `"public-orders";r=7;t=280`.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (RFC 9110 §10.2.3). Always sent with a 429.

apiKey.name: Authorization
apiKey.description: API key prefixed with `Bearer `. Alternative: the `x-api-key` header with the raw key. Available scopes: `read` and `write` (see `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`).
